output_json.summary: The patch adds a root-cause containment check (validateZipEntryDestination) in InputStreamHelper.processZipStream, called immediately after `File file = new File(dir, entry.getName())` and before any of the three sinks (mkdirsQuietly(file) for directory entries, mkdirsQuietly(parent) for file entries, and FileOutputStream(file)). It canonicalizes both `dir` and the resolved `file` and throws IOException unless the entry path is `dir` itself or a strict descendant, which blocks the Zip Slip / CWE-22 path traversal (including absolute-path entries and symlink-based escapes, since getCanonicalPath resolves real paths). Independently reran the POV and regression commands via the Docker wrapper against the current worktree state (patch applied): the original PoV (ZipSlipPovTest) now fails with the expected IOException ("Zip entry is outside of the target directory"), confirming the vulnerability no longer reproduces. The new InputStreamHelperTest (4 tests covering simple traversal, nested/mid-path traversal, directory-entry traversal, and a legitimate non-traversal extraction) passes, and `mvn -B -DskipTests package` builds cleanly. The diff is minimal and scoped: only InputStreamHelper.java (22 lines, single new private helper + one call site) was modified in product code, plus a new test file — no unrelated changes, no weakening/removal of legitimate extraction functionality, and the PoV itself was not modified or disabled.
